facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on her extremities
no remarkable medical or family history
not concurrently being treated with any medications
scattered, erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
a few asymptomatic brown flat papules scattered on her face
the palms, soles, and oral mucosa were not involved
Routine blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor tests disclosed no abnormal findings
Mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis
Atrophy of the epidermis
Well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer
Individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

concepts.why: The presence of well-developed cornoid lamellae, individual cell dyskeratosis, and atrophy of the epidermis are characteristic histopathological features of Darier disease, which is supported by the patient's clinical presentation of pruritic papules.

The combination of mild hyperkeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, along with a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes, is consistent with Grover disease, a condition characterized by transient acantholytic dermatosis.

The patient's presentation of scattered, erythematous, annular papules, along with the histopathological finding of well-developed cornoid lamellae, is consistent with disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis, a condition characterized by multiple, small, annular lesions.

rationales.F01: Rapidly spreading pruritic papules suggest a skin condition with an inflammatory component, which is consistent with Darier disease and Grover disease.
rationales.F04: Erythematous annular papules are a common feature of Darier disease and Grover disease.
rationales.F05: Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face are not typical of Darier disease, but can be seen in other conditions.
rationales.F08: Mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis is a characteristic histopathological feature of Darier disease and Grover disease.
rationales.F10: Well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer are a distinctive feature of Darier disease and Grover disease.
